key_responsibilities: Design, build, and operate innovative products and services
Design and develop scalable solutions using cloud-native architectures and microservices
Build resilient distributed systems that are scalable, fault-tolerant, and cost-effective
Leverage GenAI and AI-powered tools to enhance development productivity
Agile environments with CI/CD practices including on-call duties
Operational excellence through monitoring, troubleshooting, resolving production issues
location: Seattle, WA (+ AZ, CA, CO, GA, IL, MA, MD, MI, MN, NJ, NY, OR, PA, TN, TX, VA, WI)

llm_analysis.llm_verdict: Partial Fit (Strong for the embedded lane, weak against the generic cloud SDE description)
strengths: Embedded Systems is an explicitly listed specialization on this req - validates applying with an embedded resume
C++ depth is real and defensible: STM32 bare-metal (GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1, 3.68KB Flash), two-link IK on Arduino in C++, custom CUDA C++ kernels for VGG16
Debugging complex systems is genuinely backed: resolved 11 integration failures in COFFIN (false positives, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture)

Distributed-systems thinking exists but is HPC/edge flavored: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley (10.49x speedup, load-imbalance characterization), parallel ray tracer (4 work-distribution strategies), COFFIN three-layer WebSocket pipeline
Version control (Git/GitLab) and project experience clear the preferred bar
real_gaps: Zero AWS / cloud platform experience - the JD's core described work is cloud-native architectures and microservices
No production service ownership: no CI/CD, no on-call, no monitoring/troubleshooting of live production issues
DSA depth is the real interview risk - Amazon's new-grad loop is DSA-heavy plus Leadership Principles behavioral
overstated_by_keywords: 'data structures / algorithms' scored as covered because the basic qual is trivially low; candidate's own defensibility notes flag DSA as an active gap. 100% paper match != loop readiness.
'distributed systems' - MPI/HPC and a WebSocket edge pipeline are NOT cloud microservices with fault tolerance; adjacent, not equivalent. Do not oversell in interview.
llm_analysis.reasoning: Keyword match hits 100% only because the basic qualifications are near-trivial (one language + DSA/OOP + a STEM degree), so the number carries almost no signal. Against the JD's actual described work - cloud-native microservices, fault-tolerant distributed services, AWS, CI/CD, on-call - the profile is a weak content match. The real value is that this req explicitly names Embedded Systems as a declarable specialization, which is a legitimate door into the exact work the recruiter pitched. Apply is a clear yes; the binding constraint is not eligibility or the resume, it is DSA readiness for the loop.
